571.t: Where Buddy Petit's last jobs took place, and his real name
571.s: The interviewer cites two books on the picnic where Buddy Petit played last. Lewis corrects it and they discuss his real name, Crawford.
571.q: You better, you better, there wasn't no picnic until a child. Third, second, third, fourth of July. Goddamn, look, don't you betcha anymore, yeah? Yeah? You get out there? Yeah. Uh, no, it wasn't, it wasn't no picnic. We had played, uh, Longstoker, 48, two singles, uh, uh, Ernest Milton, myself,…

571.t: Buddy Petit's last jobs at Empire and his death
571.s: Lewis tells how Petit played the last jobs at Empire, drank at a speakeasy, fell ill and was dead when the band returned.
571.q: Well, he had been playing a little job off and on with that group of men, because, uh, it really wasn't an organized band.

571.t: Dating Buddy Petit's death by Louis Armstrong's visits
571.s: Interviewer and Lewis try to pin down the year, linking it to Louis Armstrong's visits in 1931 and to Chris Kelly's funeral.
571.q: I was 31. He came down here twice. I mean, the first time he came down here, Keenan Fender was very popular. And, uh, had a saxophone player with a thing. I never saw him. All I could hear him say, hold it out. They hold that one note, which is, uh, Andrew Martin. And, uh, the next time he came…

571.s: They talk about his burial in St. Louis Cemetery and how to find the vault.
571.q: I was in the same cemetery, and look at my real host. They didn't know name on the upgrade. No. She's buried right up there. I was in the same cemetery.

571.t: Little Dad, ill and hard of hearing
571.s: Allen reports that Little Dad is bedridden. Lewis recalls playing with him in the Humphrey and Buddy Petit bands; he could hear the beat but could not tune his banjo.
571.q: Well, he never could hear. Never could hear. I played with him a lot. During the time with, uh, Earl Humphrey, and Buddy Petit, and Eric Scott, that fellow. He always was hard of hearing, but he could hear the beat. Of course, he was a much younger man. He could hear the beat. But, uh, he couldn't…

875.t: Buddy Petit's funeral and the two bands
875.s: Howard recalls playing Petit's funeral with Eureka and his own brass band around 1931.
875.q: Well, we were at clarinet and I just remember all the fellas, it's been so long time before. Twenty years. But I know George was there. Jim was there. Little Jim at that time, he was playing the tuba. Playing the tuba. Yeah.

875.t: Buddy Petit's band, funeral and relatives
875.s: Howard did not hear Petit's sidemen, recalls the funeral bands, and points to Petit's brother Sonny as a source.
875.q: No, in fact, I never had a chance to listen to them because most of the time when they were working, we were working at the same time. So we couldn't get to each other that way, you see. And when he came back home, well, he worked it in a way he could get a job or, if he got a job, he just hired…

871.t: Buddy Petit's illness and death across the lake
871.s: Petit lost his health to tuberculosis across Lake Pontchartrain and died there; Bigard only played jobs with him there.
871.q: The drummer would be right up near the driver then, the front end of the truck? Yes. The bass player would be on the end. Back at the tailgate. Yeah, tailgate. Him and the tri-roll. I was going to ask. Some more about Buddy Petit. The other night we talked to Sammy Penn, the drummer who used to…

864.t: Playing with Buddy Petit and his illness
864.s: Tillman played jitney dances and country work with Buddy Petit, who was weak and sick; he blames exposure and hard drinking for early deaths among musicians.
864.q: Well I played with Buddy there. I had been playing in the band. We had been getting a whole lot of work over the lake around Madisonville and Maddenville all over there. He came from over there around Maddenville. Somewhere over there. And he was well known. People liked him you know. And I was…

570.t: Travels with Buddy Petit and his strokes
570.s: They travelled to Chicago and Texas; Petit's first stroke affected his hand and mouth, the second killed him; Penn was with him about five years.
570.q: Well, uh, we went to Chicago and, uh, went to Texas and all about different places. I was with him when he took the last stroke he died in a cupboard. That's the way he died.

49.t: Hardy's last playing, the gift of his horn and his funeral
49.s: At Hardy's birthday he plays the blues with his mother, gives Hazel his cornet, and dies soon after; a huge funeral crosses by ferry.
49.ch: Emmett Hardy, Bix and the Rhythm Kings
49.q: He didn't touch the horn. He gave me the horn. That's how I come and start playing the corner. When he, when he, when he, he gave me, yeah, well we, uh, it was his, uh, it was his, uh, 21st birthday. And in, in the meantime, uh, uh, the Eckert band had, had split up. Uh, half of the band went with…

638.t: Buddy Petit's style, illness and funeral
638.s: He recalls Buddy Petit's playing, his sickness and sudden death, and the funeral band assembled for it.
638.q: Oh, he had a nice style. He had a different style from any of them. But he had a nice style. He had a real nice style of playing trumpet. And he was a good musician. But he got on sick and he just kept sick, sick. Feel better. He tried to play a job. He'd go out, they'd have to bring him home sick.…

766.t: Buddy Petit in his band and his death
766.s: Buddy Petit played second trumpet with him and died on a July 4th; Milton went for him that morning.
766.q: a little before Buddy Petit. Buddy Petit was playing with me too. He worked with me too. Oh and in your band then? That's right. He was playing second trumpet with me. Buddy Petit. When he died Buddy Petit died on the 4th of July. That he was supposed to go away with me that morning. When I went to…

300.t: Leaving in 1931 and when Buddy Petit died
300.s: Humphrey left March 31, 1931, Petit was still alive then, and he only heard of the death after returning in 1941.
300.q: soon after I left. I don't know exactly when he died, but he was around a good while after I left.

574.s: Robinson sometimes played with Petit; Petit died suddenly before a job with Milton.
574.q: Yeah, sometime I worked with him, but I never just played in his band. I used to play extra sometimes. Yeah, exactly. And we used to hire him plenty of times. Because with this little band here, or this last band I played, Ernest Milton. But that's where Buddy was playing second con with the Ernest…

641.t: Buddy Petit's death and meeting Louis in Washington in 1933
641.s: Joe never tracked old Baton Rouge friends and first learned of Buddy Petit's death when he met Louis in 1933 at the Remington ferry through Pops Foster.
641.q: No, I never... I never really kept track of those guys then. The first I heard of Buddy Petit dying was when I first met Louis. In 1933 I met Louis on the
